title: Phone screen: Jane Doe (SRE candidate)
summary: Initial phone screen for SRE candidate. Covered background, recent on-call experience, familiarity with distributed systems and inference-serving concepts. Agreed to a follow-up technical exercise if references check out.
topics: next steps: technical exercise and references
next_steps: Schedule take-home evaluation call week of 2024-11-11
action_items: Maya Roberts: email candidate the take-home exercise (due 2024-11-05)
Liam Chen: draft evaluation rubric for take-home exercise (due 2024-11-07)
Jane Doe: provide two references and confirm availability for follow-up (ASAP)
transcript:
Header: Date: 2024-11-03 15:12 PST | Duration: 38 min | Attendees: Maya Roberts (Redwood), Liam Chen (Redwood), Jane Doe (Candidate)

00:00 Maya: Hi Jane, thanks for taking the time — this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I’m on the SRE team. Can you hear me okay?
00:05 Jane: Yes, thanks for having me, I can hear you fine.
01:10 Maya: Great, why don't you start with a quick summary of your recent role at Acme Analytics and what you owned there?
01:35 Jane: Sure. I was the on-call SRE for a self-serve analytics product. My focus was on latency-sensitive pipelines, autoscaling, and incident response. I led a project to reduce tail latency by about 25% by changing batching and optimizing the queueing layer.
03:02 Liam: When you say batching changes, can you give a rough example — was it changing batch-size heuristics or adding priority queues?
03:20 Jane: It was a mix. We tuned batching heuristics and added small-size priority queues for interactive traffic which helped. We also added adaptive timeouts so low-priority batches would not delay high-priority ones.
05:45 Maya: Nice. How do you approach incident postmortems? Any tooling you prefer?
06:05 Jane: We used a standard template — timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions. For tooling we used a mix of our incident tracker, Grafana dashboards, and saved query logs. I usually lead the timeline reconstruction and coordinate mitigations.
09:30 Liam: Have you worked on model-serving or inference platforms specifically? Terms like KV cache, streaming disconnects, or cold-starts ring a bell?
09:50 Jane: I haven't worked on LLM inference specifically, but I’ve handled similar issues in feature-serving: cache warming, cold-start latencies, and streaming timeouts for websockets. I'm comfortable with concepts even if not the exact models.
12:12 Maya: Ok, good. Tell us about a time you debugged a production 5xx spike under load.
12:30 Jane: We saw a spike caused by a cascading retry loop and an overloaded downstream. I introduced rate-limiting and circuit breakers, added more fine-grained metrics to isolate the caller service, and patched the retry logic.
15:50 Liam: Do you have experience with private/VPC deployments and security constraints?
16:05 Jane: Yes — Acme had a hybrid setup. I handled VPN tunnels, managed cert rotation via our internal tooling, and worked with compliance for audit logging.
18:30 Maya: What's your comfort with Linux kernel tuning / network namespaces / iptables?
18:45 Jane: I'm comfortable — I routinely tuned net.core settings, TCP buffers, and used namespaces to isolate test traffic. Not an expert in every kernel internals but sufficient for SRE tasks.
21:00 Maya: How do you prioritize reliability trade-offs against cost and latency?
21:10 Jane: I look at SLOs and cost per request. If small changes yield big latency wins with minimal cost, they get prioritized. Otherwise, we run a cost-benefit analysis with stakeholders.
24:05 Liam: Any red flags in your references we should be aware of?
24:15 Jane: I don't think so. I'm happy to share two references; one is my manager and one is a cross-functional PM.
26:40 Maya: What's your ideal notice period/availability and compensation band expectations?
26:55 Jane: I can start after a 3-week notice. Compensation: open to market.
29:10 Maya: OK. We'll send a technical exercise — it should be a short take-home focusing on debugging/logging and a small systems-design prompt. Are you comfortable with that?
29:30 Jane: Yes, that's fine.
31:00 Liam: Any questions for us about the role or team?
31:10 Jane: Yeah — how big is the SRE team, and what’s the on-call cadence?
31:25 Maya: It's a 6-person SRE team, rotations are 1 week on-call, 1 week backup. We try to keep paged tasks lightweight.
33:20 Jane: Sounds good.
35:05 Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the exercise and next steps. Thanks for your time.
35:20 Jane: Thank you, have a good day.
35:45 End of call.

Notes: Transcript contains typical transcription noise; proper nouns may be slightly off.
